title: Mara and the Provision
premise: Noor Thornbury, a disgraced railroad engineer hauling a debt across the river country, salvages a chest stamped with the seal of Vessia, a nation erased from every map she owns. Inside is a provision ledger that grants its bearer claim to the closed lines — and to the water rights feeding them. Hunted by the Consortium that erased Vessia, Noor follows a dying river upstream with an exiled cartographer and a boy who remembers too much, discovering the 'forbidden source' is a dammed archive where the Consortium buried not just water but an entire people's records. At the source she must choose: sell the provision back to her creditors and clear her debt, or breach the dam and flood the lowlands to restore what was stolen. She breaches it, drowning her own past with it, and the river — and Vessia's memory — runs free.
about_author: Rosalind Kavanagh is a former hydrological surveyor who spent a decade mapping rivers that no longer appear on official charts. She writes adventure fiction from a houseboat on the northern waterways.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Broke and dodging creditors in the port town of Sallow Bend, Noor takes a salvage contract dredging the river shallows and pulls up an iron chest stamped with a seal no one recognizes. The emotional beat is weary pragmatism curdling into unease as the harbor master goes pale at the sight of it.

chapters.title: A Dead Nation's Seal
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. An old lockkeeper identifies the mark as Vessia's and begs her to throw the chest back; instead she pries it open alone and finds the Provision, a ledger granting absolute claim to the closed rail lines and headwaters. Beat: temptation — the ledger could erase her debt in a signature.

chapters.title: Men in Gray Coats
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Consortium agents arrive in Sallow Bend asking after salvage, and Noor realizes the harbor master sold her name. She flees by night on a decommissioned line engine with the ledger sewn into her coat. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. On the abandoned rails she finds Ilya Voss, an exiled Vessian cartographer living in a signal box, who recognizes the Provision and tells her the source of the river has been dammed for thirty years. Beat: reluctant alliance; two people who trust maps more than people.

chapters.title: What the Boy Remembers
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. They shelter with river folk and meet Tam, a boy born after the erasure who nonetheless sings Vessian songs he was never taught. Ilya realizes memory survived the purge in children's rhymes. Beat: grief and fragile hope entwined.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors on the Night Train
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Her original creditors catch up, led by the courteous, ruthless Mr. Quill, who offers to buy the Provision outright. Noor stalls, lying about its location. Beat: the first taste of how much power the paper carries — and how it changes how people look at her.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The trio boards a barge convoy working the commercial channel, hiding among cargo while Consortium patrols sweep the banks. Noor teaches Tam to read from the Provision itself. Beat: found-family warmth before the storm.

chapters.title: The Drowned Station
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. The convoy passes a station half-sunk when the dam raised the waters; Ilya recognizes his own hometown beneath the surface. He confesses he helped survey the closure under duress. Beat: guilt exposed, trust cracked but holding.

chapters.title: Quill's Bargain
chapters.summary: Quill's POV. Aboard his patrol launch, Quill reflects on why the Consortium fears paper more than guns, and orders the barge convoy stopped and searched. Beat: cold institutional menace; power as paperwork.

chapters.title: Overboard
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The search nearly succeeds until Tam's singing draws a crowd of river folk who shield the fugitives; Noor escapes overboard with the ledger and loses her compass — her last tie to her old life. Beat: sacrifice, severance from the past.

chapters.title: The Marsh Archive
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. In the reed marshes they find a hidden cache of rescued Vessian documents kept by a dying archivist, who confirms the dam at the source holds not just water but the seized national records. Beat: the stakes widen — this is about memory itself.

chapters.title: What Noor Buried
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Around a marsh fire, Noor admits the truth of her disgrace: she signed off on a line closure that flooded a valley village, the same engineering logic that drowned Vessia. Beat: self-recognition; she is not so different from the men hunting her.

chapters.title: The Toll Gate
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The party passes through a Consortium toll city where Tam sees propaganda murals celebrating the erasure as 'provision.' He steals a copy of the official history to compare against the archive. Beat: righteous anger awakening in the youngest voice.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Weir
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The archivist's nephew sells their route to Quill for amnesty; at a mountain weir, Quill corners them and offers Noor her debt cleared one final time. She refuses — and watches him take Tam hostage as insurance. Beat: refusal at real cost.

chapters.title: The Ascent
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya and Noor climb the forbidden headwaters using Ilya's pre-erasure survey maps, pursued by Quill's column, racing the winter freeze that will close the passes. Beat: relentless forward motion; exhaustion transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: The Face of the Dam
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. They reach the source: a vast concrete face stamped with the Consortium crest, behind which the archive vaults are sealed into the spillways. Noor reads the Provision aloud and discovers its final clause — the bearer may dissolve the provision entirely. Beat: awe and dread; the choice crystallizes.

chapters.title: Quill's Truth
chapters.summary: Quill's POV. Quill arrives with Tam and reveals the Consortium's secret: the erasure was never about rebellion but about water — whoever holds the source holds every downstream nation. He offers Noor partnership. Beat: the corruption of power made explicit, and almost persuasive.

chapters.title: The Breach
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Climax. Noor signs the dissolution clause, voiding all claims including her own debt, and fires the spillway charges Ilya rigged. The dam groans; Quill tries to stop her and falls into the flood he helped create; Tam is swept free. Beat: irreversible action, terror and release.

chapters.title: Water Finds Its Level
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The flood roars down the valley, taking bridges and borders with it, and the river folk read it as deliverance. Tam recites Vessian songs to crowds gathering on the levees. Beat: chaos becoming renewal through the child's witness.

chapters.title: The Republic of Paper
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Weeks later, salvaged archives surface downstream; towns declare themselves provisionally Vessian again. Ilya begins drawing the first new map of the country, leaving blank spaces on purpose. Beat: cautious hope; memory rebuilt, not restored.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Debtless and unemployed, Noor declines offers to administer the new water councils and instead takes a contract surveying reopened lines — with Tam apprenticed beside her. Beat: quiet resolution; belonging chosen rather than claimed.

chapters.title: Source
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, coda. A year on, Noor returns to the breached dam and finds spring water running clean through the broken concrete. She leaves her repaired compass on the stone. Beat: peace; the river, like memory, needs no keeper.
